methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the focus was on extracting the core requirements and constraints of the dual-edge triggered flip-flop emulation. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the described logic functions, implementation details, and timing considerations. The goal was to create sets of atomic units that could be compared to assess the coverage and similarity between the original topic and the generated specification.

spec_atomic_units: Implement dual-edge triggered flip-flop using combinational logic and single-edge triggered flip-flops
Use two single-edge triggered flip-flops (positive and negative edge-triggered)
Combine outputs of flip-flops using an XOR gate
q = p ^ n (where p is positive-edge flip-flop output and n is negative-edge flip-flop output)
Registers p and n are updated using non-blocking assignments (<=
p <= d ^ n (updated on positive edge of clk)
n <= d ^ p (updated on negative edge of clk)
Output q is the XOR of p and n
Critical path involves propagation delay through combinational logic and clock-to-q delay of internal flip-flops
Setup time for input d with respect to rising and falling edges of clk is critical
